_note: Engine-only settings. Every threshold, weight, utility bound and tolerance of the missions lives in mission_scoring.json and is NOT repeated here. Each setting has a value and a why; every one is also listed in /ASSUMPTIONS.md with its effect on results.

engine_version.why: Version of the engine code that produced a bundle; written into manifest.json so a bundle can be traced to the code. The package's __version__ is read from here. 3.1.0: the similarity rule is a per-mission setting; Rover and Solar panels use the real-value rule real_value_tolerance (team decision of 2026-11-15, morning); Lunar base keeps zone_twin unchanged. 3.0.0: three offered missions (rover, solar, lunar_base), the step-by-step funnel export, the repository's own similarity (analog_finder) behind the similarity_rule setting, tiled per-cell detail files. 2.0.0: dataset descriptors, the real 1-degree tables, the v2 binary bundle. 1.1.0: review fixes.

mission_config.why: The team's new filter system. All gates, soft weights, bad/good bounds and category tables come from this file.

missions.why: Team lead decision 1 (2026-11-14): exactly three missions are offered, in this order: rover, solar and lunar_base. lunar_base is an exact copy of the thermal block of mission_scoring.json (checked at load time and by a test); thermal and ice stay in that file untouched as components of lunar_base (mission_scoring.json lunar_base.components) and are not offered as missions. The ice component is evaluated on every Earth cell and exported as information only: it never changes the lunar_base ranking. The JSON's own 'offered_missions' list must equal this one.

elevation_m.reason: The common gate elevation_m >= 1 is a land mask written for Earth (its why says 'solo tierra firme, descarta oceano, que el modelo fija en -250 m'). Lunar elevation_m is height relative to a datum (LOLA, 1737.4 km sphere), so on the Moon the same gate would remove 11,041 of 16,200 cells for no physical reason (audit A3 section 2). On the real 1-degree table lunar elevation_m is above the 1737.4 km sphere too and 43,502 of 64,800 lunar cells are below 1 m (real_data/README.md), so the gate stays Earth-only there as well.

mask_fraction.reason: Kept on both bodies exactly as written. On the Moon mask_fraction is the constant 1.0, so the gate never removes a lunar cell. On the real Earth table mask_fraction is the land share of the cell (ESA CCI land cover; inland water counts as water), so the gate means 'at least 30 % land'.

gate_body_applicability.why: Which body each COMMON gate applies to. Thresholds are untouched; only applicability is set here. Mission gates always apply to both bodies. Pending team confirmation.

on_invalid_value.why: A value outside its physically valid range is reported in validity.json and flagged on the cell; it is never clipped, replaced or silently fixed. With today's data no value fails.

value.population: all cells of both bodies that pass the mission's hard filters (concatenated, each cell counted once)

similarity_scale.why: Per-variable physical scale for sim = max(0, 1 - |earth - moon| / scale). A pooled robust physical range keeps real Earth-Moon differences visible: per-body z-scores or percentile ranks would score Earth's largest MODELLED thermal amplitude (38.75 K, formula 8 + 22*bare + 0.0022*elev) as a perfect match for the MODELLED lunar values (63-180 K, formula 180*cos(lat)^0.35). Both ranges are formula output, and the lunar one is contradicted by Diviner (about 250-300 K at low and mid latitudes, R2 section 3; 95-390 K at the equator and about 220 K at polar rims, R3 F10/F12). The population is all passing cells of both bodies concatenated, so the body with more passing cells sets most of the scale (thermal: 16,200 lunar against 2,613 Earth cells); this is pending team confirmation. The rover 'tolerances' in mission_scoring.json are not used as scales because they are defined for 300 m baselines and the *_300m_* columns are copies of 2-degree-cell values.

similarity_zero_scale.why: If a pooled range is zero (every passing cell has the same value), sim is 1 when the two values are equal and 0 otherwise, instead of dividing by zero.

mix_factor.why: alpha in mission_scoring.combine_with_similarity: final = alpha * similarity_pct + (1 - alpha) * suitability. 0.5 is that function's own default (mission_scoring.py line 207). Adopting the library default is still a decision on an open question (how much lunar likeness against mission fitness), so it is pending team confirmation; ASSUMPTIONS.md section 3 gives the effect of 0.3 and 0.7 on each mission's top 10.

pairing_chunk_rows.why: Number of Earth cells compared with all candidate lunar cells per vectorised block. Performance and memory only; it does not change results (the twin is an argmax per Earth row). 128 rows x 64,800 lunar cells x 8 bytes = 66 MB per temporary array on the 1-degree grid; 512 needed 265 MB per array.

value.body_rule: weighted mean of level_scores over the mission's weighted variables that have data, using the mission's soft weights
value.pair_rule: min(Earth score, Moon score) * coverage, where coverage = share of the mission's soft weight with data on both cells

confidence.why: Confidence must say how much the numbers behind a ranking can be trusted. A MEASURED value counts fully, a DERIVED one (a stated formula on a measured value) a little less, an UNDOCUMENTED cached array less, and a MODELLED formula least. The weaker body limits the pair. The criteria act at rover-to-site scale, so a cell larger than high_max_cell_km (every 2-degree cell: about 222 km on Earth, about 61 km on the Moon; every 1-degree cell: about 111 km and 30 km) can never be 'high'. A variable counts on a body only where that body's cell has a value; coverage is the share of the soft weight with data on both the Earth cell and its twin.

explain_top_n.why: Number of top-ranked Earth cells per mission written with a full per-variable explanation in explain.json; enough for a top-N panel and small on disk.

top_failure_reasons_n.why: Number of commonest failure reasons per mission and body listed in missions.json.

body_radius_km.why: Mean radii used for the true cell size (2*pi*R/180 per 2 degrees) and for great-circle distances. 1737.4 km is the sphere of the LOLA DEM and of the IAU gazetteer .prj; 6371.0 km is the IUGG mean Earth radius.

lunar_gazetteer_csv.why: Offline extract of the USGS/IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature (MOON_nomenclature_center_pts, 9,087 features, longitudes 0-360 positive east) made by 'python -m engine gazetteer'. Source file and hash are in engine/data/iau_source.json.

lunar_feature_exclude_types.why: Satellite features are lettered craters named after a parent (e.g. 'Tycho K'); 7,064 of 9,087 entries. Excluding them labels a cell with a primary named feature, which is what a map reader recognises (audit A4 used the same rule for 'nearest primary').

antarctic_label_lat_max.why: reverse_geocoder returns the nearest populated GeoNames place, and there are none in Antarctica, so cells there were labelled 'TF Kerguelen' or 'ZA' (audit A3). Land cells whose centre is at or south of 60 S (the Antarctic Treaty area) are labelled Antarctica (AQ) instead, with no first-level region.

export_decimals.why: Rounding of floats in the bundle. Utilities and per-variable similarities are published with 6 decimals and the engine computes suitability, similarity and the final score from exactly these published values, so the browser reproduces them with the DATA_CONTRACT formulas to about 1e-4 points. Scores are published with 2 decimals and the rank is computed on the published final score (ties by id), so the stored rank follows the contract rule on stored values. Other keys keep the input precision of the CSV (variable values), the IAU gazetteer's precision (iau_lat_lon, diameter_km) and the soft weights (weight). The bundle stays under 12 MB.

mission_titles.why: Short English titles for the app. The team's own descriptions in mission_scoring.json are exported verbatim as 'description'. lunar_base is the lunar base mission whose core is the thermal-endurance configuration.

similarity_comparability.why: A variable that the dataset's registry marks as not the same physical quantity on the two bodies (legacy: provenance.json comparable_across_bodies = false; real tables: datasets.json comparability status 'not_comparable') is left out of the Earth-Moon similarity and of the twin search; it still counts fully in suitability. 'comparable_with_caveat' variables are used and their reason is exported. Comparing bare-ground fraction with a lunar value set by definition, or an Earth air temperature with a lunar surface temperature, would make 'Moon-likeness' measure something else. Pending team confirmation; set false to compare every weighted variable with data on both bodies.

explain_helps_n.why: Number of variables listed in explain.json 'helps_most' (largest final points): enough for a one-line 'why' in the panel.

explain_hurts_n.why: Number of variables listed in explain.json 'hurts_most' (largest lost points above 0).

coordinate_tolerance_deg.why: Largest difference, in degrees, accepted by the schema between a CSV lat/lon and the cell centre computed from row/col. The CSV stores centres with float rounding only; 1e-6 deg is about 0.1 m on Earth.

earth_country_polygons.why: Country of an Earth land cell by point-in-polygon on Natural Earth 1:110m admin-0 countries (public domain). The nearest GeoNames place gave the wrong country for 229 of 5,359 land cells inside a polygon (review). Cells outside every polygon (coasts at 110m resolution, small islands) fall back to the nearest GeoNames place. Source and sha256 in engine/data/ne_source.json.

not_used_by_engine_why.value: tolerances: defined for 300 m baselines while the *_300m_* columns are 2-degree copies. workable_days: not read by mission_scoring.py. domain weights (relieve/material/termico/luz/agua): the team note in mission_scoring.json says they are used only by the web 'Use Weights' button of the similarity; the engine instead weights the similarity with the mission's soft weights, because no mapping from these domains to the new variables exists. This departure is pending team confirmation (ASSUMPTIONS.md section 3).
not_used_by_engine_why.why: Text exported in missions.json 'not_used_by_engine.why' so the app can say why these team settings have no effect.

missing_data_reason.why: A cell whose gated or required variable is empty is eliminated (mission_scoring.json on_missing_gate = 'drop'). The reason code is '<variable>:missing' (as in the v1 bundle and the tests) and the interface label is 'no data: <variable>', so the app can count how many cells each mission loses to missing data (for example Antarctica has no land surface temperature in the real tables).

binary_encoding.why: v2 binary columns: little-endian Float32 (NaN = missing) for cell values and Int32 for everything else, with -2147483648 (INT32_MIN, never a valid value here) as the missing sentinel. Utilities, per-variable similarities, scores and confidence scores are stored as Int32 q with value = q / 10^decimals, using the same decimals as export_decimals, so the browser decodes exactly the published value the engine computed with (a Float32 of 0.123456 is not 0.123456 and would break the exact recompute).

first_view_budget_bytes.why: Size targets of the v2 bundle (2.5 MB = 2,500,000 bytes for manifest, missions, variables, places, Earth base and the default mission; 14 MB = 14,000,000 bytes in total, decimal megabytes so the target holds under either reading), set for loading on a phone. The build reports the sizes and the tests check them; nothing is cut silently to meet them.

rover.text: Provisional: the rover block of mission_scoring.json says its gates and tolerances were migrated as they were and its soft criteria approximate the old formula until Robotics 1 provides the final one (the block's 'provisional' text is exported verbatim).

solar.text: Team design values: the solar thresholds have no external source (mission_scoring.json note: 'Umbrales de solar y thermal = valores de diseno NO validados con fuente externa').

lunar_base.text: Team design values: lunar_base is the thermal block, whose thresholds have no external source (mission_scoring.json note: 'Umbrales de solar y thermal = valores de diseno NO validados con fuente externa').

mission_threshold_status.why: Team lead decision 1: rover is shown as provisional (its JSON block says so) and the solar and thermal thresholds are team design values with no external source (the JSON note says so). Both labels are carried into missions.json so the app shows them next to every number of the mission.

similarity_rule.why: Team decision of 2026-11-15 (morning), given by the team lead's delegate on the team lead's behalf, answering docs/ANALOG_PRINCIPLE.md (docs/DECISIONS.md section 'Decisiones tomadas (15-11-2026, mañana)'): the similarity rule is a per-mission setting. Rover and Solar panels use real_value_tolerance (similarity on real values within stated tolerances, real_value_similarity). Lunar base keeps zone_twin exactly as shipped before (z-scores on the nine NASA regions) until the team confirms a new proposal. Earlier: zone_twin for all three missions (team decision of 2026-11-15, answer 1 to docs/DECISIONS.md), before that repo_global_mean (team lead decision 4, 2026-11-14). A plain string applies one rule to every mission; '--similarity-rule RULE' does that for one build (repo_global_mean, zone_twin and physical_pooled stay available and tested).

value.repo_global_mean: What the repository does by default (analog_finder.compute_analog_ranking with its default target zone 'Global Lunar Surface Mean'): the target is the mean z profile of the whole Moon; one similarity per Earth cell, the same for every mission; no twin. Kept available for comparison; not the shipped rule since 2026-11-15.
value.zone_twin: Active for lunar_base (team decision of 2026-11-15; for rover and solar until the morning decision of the same day): z-score formula of analog_finder against every lunar cell of the mission's zone (similarity_zones); the twin is the single most similar zone cell (ties: lowest id). Lunar cells are not passed through the mission filters.
value.physical_pooled: The integration's earlier rule (engine 1.1-2.0): per-variable sim = max(0, 1 - |earth - moon| / pooled 5-95 percentile range) over the mission's comparable weighted variables, twin among the lunar cells passing the mission. Kept available, not the default.
value.real_value_tolerance: Active for rover and solar since the team decision of 2026-11-15 (morning): per variable a score exp(-0.5 * (|earth - moon| / tolerance)^2) on REAL values; similarity = 100 * weighted mean of the scores; pair filter: every key variable within its tolerance and every secondary within twice its tolerance, otherwise no twin; twin = the zone cell passing the filter with the highest similarity (ties: lowest id). Variables, roles, weights, tolerances and zones in real_value_similarity.

similarity_rule_options.why: What each value of similarity_rule means; exported in similarity.json so the app can say which rule produced the numbers of each mission.

value.features_and_weights: analog_finder.ANALOG_FEATURES and analog_finder.DEFAULT_WEIGHTS, imported at build time (not copied)

repo_similarity.why: Team lead decision 3: similarity is computed with the repository's own formula. decay 0.45 is the constant of compute_analog_ranking ('similarity_pct = 100.0 * np.exp(-0.45 * rms_dist)'); the Earth population is its land filter ('earth_df["elevation_m"] > 0.0'); the Moon is normalised over all its cells as the function does. zero_variation_threshold is the function's own scale threshold (normalize_planetary_features falls back to the std, then to 1, when a scale is <= 1e-6); it is used only to REPORT variables with zero or near-zero variation on a body (similarity.json variation), never to drop one silently. z-scores are rounded to 4 decimals and similarity_pct to 2 by the function itself (np.round); the bundle stores exactly those published values. A test runs analog_finder.compute_analog_ranking on the legacy table and checks the engine's similarity equals its similarity_pct on every land cell.

lunar_base.name: NASA Artemis III candidate landing regions (9, announced 2024-10-28)
lunar_base.source: USGS navigational grids (McClernan 2024, DOI 10.5066/P1MEQ6UK, CC0): each region's footprint is the union of its 1 km grid squares, an upper bound of the region (the exact outline file is not published)

similarity_zones.why: Team lead decision 4 (zone_twin only): rover and solar target the south-pole zone exactly as the code defines it (centre latitude at or below -75). lunar_base targets the lunar cells that intersect NASA's nine Artemis III candidate landing regions (announced 2024-10-28) from the USGS data release (DOI 10.5066/P1MEQ6UK; the exact outlines are not published, so each footprint is the union of the region's 1 km navigational grid squares, an upper bound), if a verified region file is present in the repository (engine/data/artemis_iii_regions.geojson: GeoJSON in planetocentric degrees, longitude -180..180 east-positive, top-level 'verified': true, copied from the proposal agent's verified outlines); otherwise the south-pole zone (never the global mean). The zone used and the reason are written to similarity.json. Lunar cells are not passed through the mission filters. Confirmed by the team on 2026-11-15 (rover and solar stay on the south-pole zone, the branch's version from analog_finder.py commit ff6f1ae, not Tycho; lunar_base on the nine NASA regions).

twin_tie_rule.why: zone_twin: when two zone cells are at exactly the same distance (double precision) from an Earth cell, the one with the lowest lunar cell id is the twin, so the result does not depend on processing order.

detail_tile_rows.why: Per-cell funnel detail (utilities, z-scores, the ice component) is split into files of this many grid rows (18 files on the 180-row grid), so the app loads about one eighteenth of the detail to show any land cell instead of every mission file. Layout only; no effect on results.

similarity_meaning.text: Each Earth point is paired with its lunar twin: the single 1-degree lunar cell, inside the mission's target zone, that holds the most similar relative position on the Moon as the Earth point holds on Earth (slope, roughness, relative elevation and surface temperature, each compared within its own world). A high similarity means 'same place in each world's range', not 'same values': both sets of values are shown side by side.
similarity_meaning.where: lunar_base only (zone_twin rule): wherever a similarity is shown, next to the absolute values of every similarity variable on Earth (earth_base.bin v.<column>) and on the Moon (twins.json values)

similarity_meaning_real_values.text: Each Earth point is paired with its lunar twin: the 1-degree lunar cell, inside the mission's target zone, whose real values are closest. Similarity is computed on real values within stated tolerances: every key variable of the twin is within its tolerance of the Earth point and every secondary variable within twice its tolerance, and each variable scores lower the further apart the two values are. Both values and their difference are shown side by side.
similarity_meaning_real_values.where: rover and solar (real_value_tolerance rule): wherever a similarity is shown, next to each similarity variable's Earth value, lunar value, difference and tolerance (earth_<mission>_pairs.bin '<variable>.earth', '<variable>.moon', '<variable>.diff'; tolerances in missions.json similarity.variables)

rock_note.text: Bare-ground fraction is shown for information only. It is not part of the similarity: on the Moon it is 1 everywhere by definition, so it cannot tell lunar places apart.
rock_note.where: next to the bare-ground fraction (rock_or_bare_frac) of both points

missing_temperature_mark.text: no temperature data: similarity computed with 3 variables
missing_temperature_mark.where: lunar_base only (rover and solar no longer use temperature in the similarity): on every pair whose similarity used fewer variables because temperature is missing (earth_<mission>.bin sim_missing_bits has the temp_k bit), in the panel and in the ranking list

missing_temperature_note.text: No surface temperature here: the satellite climatology we use does not cover Antarctica. This twin was chosen on relief only (slope, roughness, relative elevation), so its similarity is not comparable with points that include temperature.
missing_temperature_note.where: lunar_base only: in the panel of those points

twin_sharing_note.text: This lunar twin is shared by N Earth points (X % of the ranked points for this mission). The lunar base zone is small (280 cells), cold and rugged, so a few gentle cells are the best match for most places on Earth.
twin_sharing_note.where: next to the twin; N = twins.json earth_cells (or moon_<mission>.bin twin_count), X = 100 * N / missions.json ranked_count (the paired points). The second sentence is about lunar_base; for rover and solar show the first sentence only

placeholders.X: their share of the mission's ranked points, in percent

no_twin_note.text: No lunar analog: no cell of the mission's lunar zone has {variable} within {bound} {unit} of this point (closest: {gap} {unit} away). The point keeps its suitability; it has no similarity and no final score.
no_twin_note.where: rover and solar: on every passing point without a twin (earth_<mission>.bin twin missing), in the panel and the ranking list (listed after the paired points by suitability)

placeholders.variable: label of missions.json similarity.variables[k] where k = earth_<mission>_pairs.bin nopair_var
placeholders.gap: earth_<mission>_pairs.bin nopair_gap (the smallest gap found), with 2 decimals rounded UP (ceil), so a gap just above the bound never displays as equal to the bound (rover: 30.02 m against a 30 m bound)

no_twin_note.variant_no_joint_match: No lunar analog: every variable alone has a close lunar cell, but no single cell of the zone is within the bounds for all of them at once (closest: {variable} {gap} {unit} away, bound {bound} {unit}). The point keeps its suitability; it has no similarity and no final score.
no_twin_note.variant_note: use variant_no_joint_match when nopair_kind is 'no_joint_match' (missions.json similarity.nopair_kinds)

solar_limitation.replaces: the solar limitation of decision 5 (2026-11-15 night), superseded: the solar twin is no longer chosen by terrain and temperature
solar_limitation.text: This pair is matched on sunlight above the atmosphere: {toa_earth} kWh/m²/day at the top of Earth's atmosphere here and {toa_moon} kWh/m²/day on the lunar surface. At the Earth site only {ground_earth} of those {toa_earth} kWh/m²/day reach the ground ({loss_pct} % is lost in the atmosphere), while the Moon has no atmosphere and its day lasts {lunar_day} Earth days, about half of them in darkness. Terrain (slope and roughness) is a secondary criterion.
solar_limitation.where: on every solar pair (earth_solar.bin twin present), in the panel next to the twin

toa_earth.meaning: Earth's sunlight above the atmosphere (DERIVED, toa_insolation)

toa_moon.meaning: lunar surface irradiance of the twin

ground_earth.meaning: Earth's irradiance at the ground (earth_base.bin v.irradiance_kwh_m2_day)

loss_pct.meaning: share of the sunlight above the atmosphere that does not reach the ground at the Earth site, in percent

approved_texts.why: English web texts. similarity_meaning, rock_note, missing_temperature_mark, missing_temperature_note and twin_sharing_note: approved by the team on 2026-11-15 (answers 1 to 5 to docs/DECISIONS.md), copied verbatim from section 8 of each decision; similarity_meaning and the temperature texts now apply to lunar_base only ('missions'). similarity_meaning_real_values, no_twin_note and solar_limitation: written for the team decision of 2026-11-15 (morning; the delegate's conditions: the meaning must say that similarity is computed on real values within stated tolerances; the solar text says that the pair is matched on sunlight above the atmosphere, how much reaches the ground at the Earth site, that the lunar day lasts 29.5 Earth days and that terrain is secondary, in at most three sentences, and never says or implies that panels charge the same in both places); the solar_limitation of decision 5 is superseded. A text with 'placeholders' is a template the app fills per pair from the named file and column. Exported in similarity.json 'texts'; a text with 'mission' and 'mission_card' not false is also the first item of that mission's missions.json 'known_limitations'.

value.score: s = exp(-0.5 * (|earth value - moon value| / tolerance)^2)
value.similarity: 100 * sum(weight * s) / sum(weight) over the variables with a value on both sides, in the listed order
value.missing_key: a key variable without a value on either side fails the filter (no pair)
value.missing_secondary: a secondary variable without a value on either side is left out of the filter and of the similarity; the remaining weights are renormalised

EARTH.text: deviogram roughness at a ~1.9 km lag

MOON.text: deviogram roughness at a ~1.9 km lag

EARTH.text: elevation_m minus the area-weighted (cos latitude) mean elevation_m of every Earth cell with a value (land cells; ocean cells have no elevation_m in the real table)

MOON.text: elevation_m minus the area-weighted (cos latitude) mean elevation_m of every lunar cell

EARTH.text: annual-mean daily sunlight on a horizontal surface at the top of Earth's atmosphere, from the cell-centre latitude (toa_insolation); a formula, not a measurement

MOON.text: lunar surface irradiance of the lunar table (no atmosphere, so it is also the sunlight above the surface)

info_differences.note: Not part of the similarity: their real values on both sides and the difference are exported per pair for information (the team lead asked at 04:48 to see them).

atmosphere_comparison.why: Team condition of 2026-11-15 (morning): every solar pair also carries the Earth cell's irradiance at the ground and the share lost in the atmosphere (1 - ground / above the atmosphere).

real_value_similarity.why: Team decision of 2026-11-15 (morning), given by the team lead's delegate on the team lead's behalf, answering docs/ANALOG_PRINCIPLE.md (docs/DECISIONS.md section 'Decisiones tomadas (15-11-2026, mañana)'). Method (P1-P9 of the team lead, 2026-11-15 04:47-04:49 CET): similarity on real values with a Gaussian score per variable, key variables 80 % of the weight, pair filter key <= tolerance and secondary <= 2 x tolerance. Tolerances: rover slope 2 deg and roughness 30 m are illustrative team values (rover_preset.py version 3, 5 km baseline); relative elevation 500 m and irradiance 0.6 kWh/m2/day were set by the delegate on the team lead's behalf on 2026-11-15. Zones: rover south pole (unchanged), solar the equatorial maria of analog_finder. Temperature 10 K and amplitude 5 K are reference values only and not used. score_decimals = the published precision of the per-variable scores (int32 q / 1e6), so the browser recomputes similarity exactly.

toa_insolation.why: New DERIVED value for the solar key variable (team decision of 2026-11-15, morning): Earth's annual-mean daily sunlight on a horizontal surface at the top of the atmosphere, from latitude only, with a Kepler orbit (the checker's corrected formula, docs/ANALOG_PRINCIPLE.md 'Comprobación' item 1: mean anomaly sampled uniformly in time, so the annual mean is the same in both hemispheres). Solar constant 1361.0 W/m2: the value already cited in the provenance of the lunar irradiance (real_data/provenance_moon.csv, irradiance_kwh_m2_day: NASA NSSDC Moon fact sheet). Obliquity 23.44 deg and eccentricity 0.0167: NASA NSSDC Earth fact sheet (https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html). Sun's longitude at perihelion 282.9 deg = Earth's longitude of perihelion (102.9 deg, same fact sheet) + 180; it only shifts the season and does not change the annual mean. 3650 samples and 20 fixed-point iterations: numerical settings of the checker's code (converged far below the published 4 decimals). reference_values_kwh_m2_day are the checker's figures at 0 / 30 / 45 / 60 degrees, checked by a test.

lunar_day_earth_days.why: Length of the lunar day (synodic month) in Earth days, as cited in real_data/provenance_moon.csv (irradiance_kwh_m2_day: 'Lunar day = 29.53 Earth days'); used, rounded to one decimal, in the solar pair text the team asked for on 2026-11-15 (morning).
